subject: anatomy
title: Cerebellar anatomy, deep nuclei and functional circuits

steps.tx: The **cerebellum** occupies the posterior cranial fossa beneath the tentorium cerebelli. It comprises two lateral hemispheres joined by the midline vermis. It coordinates voluntary motor activity, maintains equilibrium and regulates muscle tone without initiating movement. Three cerebellar peduncles connect it to the brainstem: the superior peduncle connects to the midbrain, the middle peduncle connects to the pons, and the inferior peduncle connects to the medulla.
steps.say: The cerebellum occupies the posterior cranial fossa beneath the tentorium cerebelli. It comprises two lateral hemispheres joined by the midline vermis. It coordinates voluntary motor activity, maintains equilibrium and regulates muscle tone without initiating movement. Three cerebellar peduncles connect it to the brainstem: superior to midbrain, middle to pons, and inferior to medulla.

steps.tx: Four pairs of **deep cerebellar nuclei** embed within the white matter from lateral to medial: dentate, emboliform, globose and fastigial. A useful mnemonic is 'Don't Eat Greasy Food'. The large, folded dentate nucleus receives input from the lateral hemispheres and projects via the superior cerebellar peduncle to the ventrolateral nucleus of the thalamus and red nucleus to modulate motor planning.

steps.tx: The cerebellar cortex features three distinct layers. The outer **molecular layer** contains basket cells, stellate cells and parallel fibres. The middle **Purkinje layer** contains large Purkinje neurons, which provide the sole inhibitory GABAergic output of the cerebellar cortex to the deep nuclei. The inner **granular layer** contains millions of densely packed granule cells receiving excitatory mossy fibre input and projecting parallel fibres.

The middle Purkinje layer contains large Purkinje neurons, which provide the sole inhibitory GABAergic output to the deep nuclei. The inner granular layer contains millions of granule cells receiving mossy fibres.

left.title: Mossy fibres
points: Arise from spinal cord and pontine nuclei
Synapse on granule cells in glomeruli
Influence many Purkinje cells via parallel fibres

right.title: Climbing fibres
points: Arise exclusively from inferior olivary nucleus
Wind directly around Purkinje cell dendrites
Essential for motor learning and error signaling

steps.tx: Cerebellar lesions manifest with **ipsilateral ataxia** because cerebellar pathways to and from the cerebral cortex double-cross. Lesions of the midline vermis produce truncal ataxia, titubation and gait unsteadiness, commonly observed in alcoholic cerebellar degeneration. Hemispheric cerebellar lesions produce appendicular ataxia, intention tremor, dysmetria, dysdiadochokinesia and scanning speech on the same side of the body.
